borg_lunal_mode.text: The borg will dive deep in the dungeon, even while he is still low level, bouncing between levels to take nearby down stairs. Once deep, he will gather items, then recall to town. He will not recall back down into the dungeon, but walk all the way down again. If you want a fast win, this is not the option for you. If you want the borg to have maxed stats early on at the expense of game turns, then give this a try. The best way to use this is to have a borg that can cast Satisfy Hunger. This is a one way trip for the borg and he will be getting hungry. The borg should also have a perma light source (like the phial). Again, one way trip. He won't be stopping to restock his fuel source. However, if he has food or fuel, he will use them when appropriate. Having extra speed will help the borg too. Often he will come down the stairs, and find himself right next to a monster. Sometimes, that monster can get the first hit on a borg, killing him instantly. Even +3 speed would help to avoid this type of instadeath. Self Lunal Mode will allow the borg to use the stair scumming in order to dive deep in the dungeon for his own goals. For example, if the borg has been down to depth 99, and now has no more potions of healing, he will only be prepared for depth 45. He will remain shallow in the dungeon, from depth 1-10 waiting for the shops to cycle. Then he will attempt to buy a healing potion from the town shops. If none is available, he will return to the shallow dungeon depths and wait for the shops to cycle. He will repeat this pattern until he gets a potion of healing. If the borg is allowed to self-lunal, then it will bounce the stairs down to a depth where it feels comfortable. In the case above, it will do this until about depth 40.

borg_param_caution_breeder_stand_radius.text: With breeders on the level and no easy escape, stand and fight: breeders no longer make the level scary or the Borg flee, and while only breeders are near it does not retreat (#503). An easy escape is a free staircase within easy_escape_steps grids, Phase Door, teleport, Teleport Level, an escape or Word of Recall; a smaller value stands more often. Standing, with a breeder within stand_radius grids and nothing else near, it neither retreats nor backs away. 0 = C (flee breeders). Turns on the hunt below. Impact (games of 6 that play differently with the value changed to): caution_breeder_fight 0: 3; caution_breeder_easy_escape_steps 10: 1; caution_breeder_stand_radius 10: 0.

borg_param_caution_cornered.text: Cornered: no Phase Door, teleport or escape, a known monster within the radius, and danger at or above danger_tenths / 10 of the HP (#504). Then the Borg uses every buff it has (fear cure, Speed, Heroism, Berserk Strength, Blessing; spells only at or below spell_fail), reads Monster Confusion against an adjacent unique or a monster more than big_level_margin levels above it, and a melee class does not retreat. 0 = off. Lower danger_tenths or a larger radius counts it cornered sooner. Impact (games of 6 that play differently with the value changed to): caution_cornered 0: 2; caution_cornered_danger_tenths 20: 1; caution_cornered_radius 4: 0; caution_cornered_big_level_margin 1: 0; caution_cornered_spell_fail 50: 0.

borg_param_caution_rising_descend_danger.text: While rising, allow a descent again when the danger here is above avoidance x this / 10 (#483). Lower lets danger push it down sooner. Impact: set to 20, 0 of 6 test games play differently.

borg_param_caution_rising_explore_ticks.text: Walking home (rising), hold a descent that is not a desperate escape for this many Borg ticks on each level while it explores for an up staircase (#483). Higher explores longer before giving up and going down. Impact: set to 600, 1 of 6 test games play differently.

borg_param_caution_rising_hold_flee_desc.text: Walking home (rising), a flight takes no down staircase unless the danger here is at or above the HP, and that staircase is no easy escape (#557). 0 = off (C). Impact: set to 1, 1 of 6 test games play differently.

borg_param_caution_scary_afraid.text: A named-list or damage-rule scary monster that has lost this percent of its HP, or (with the flag) is afraid, scares no more: Grip fled from one flask of oil (#539). Lower calms monsters sooner; 0 and 0 = C. With the latch at 1 it only stops the level from becoming scary; at 0 it also ends the scare. Impact (games of 6 that play differently with the value changed to): caution_scary_hurt_percent 100: 0; caution_scary_afraid 0: 0.

borg_param_caution_scary_damage_percent.text: A monster is also scary when one character turn of its melee can take at least this percent of max HP: Fang is scary to a 10-HP Mage, not to an 80-HP Warrior (#505). Lower makes more monsters scary; 0 = off. Spells are not counted. Impact: set to 120, 0 of 6 test games play differently.

borg_param_caution_scary_hurt_percent.text: A named-list or damage-rule scary monster that has lost this percent of its HP, or (with the flag) is afraid, scares no more: Grip fled from one flask of oil (#539). Lower calms monsters sooner; 0 and 0 = C. With the latch at 1 it only stops the level from becoming scary; at 0 it also ends the scare. Impact (games of 6 that play differently with the value changed to): caution_scary_hurt_percent 100: 0; caution_scary_afraid 0: 0.

borg_param_caution_scary_latch.text: 1 = a scary level stays scary until a new level (the C latch). 0 = checked again each scan: with no scary monster left, the scare's leave and flee are withdrawn. Door scares stay latched. Needs caution_scary_stand (#515). Impact: set to 0, 4 of 6 test games play differently.

borg_param_caution_scary_named_monsters.text: Named scary monsters (the list below) make a level scary: the Borg leaves, flees and does not hunt (#503, #518). 0 = only the resist-based scares (nether, blindness, chaos, confusion, poison), which apply either way. Impact: set to 0, 6 of 6 test games play differently.

borg_param_caution_scary_ranged_no_stair.text: On a scary level with no reachable staircase, attack the monster with the best ranged attack before reading Recall or Phase Door (#539). 0 = C. Impact: set to 0, 2 of 6 test games play differently.

borg_param_caution_scary_stand.text: Flee a scary level only while the escape is real: a free staircase within the breeders' easy_escape_steps, an escape item, or no scary monster awake and as fast as the character. Otherwise stand and fight with the cornered buffs. A monster that never moves is never scary (#530). 0 = always flee. Impact: set to 0, 4 of 6 test games play differently.

borg_param_caution_scary_unlatch_kill.text: 1 = the level stops being scary once the last scary monster known was killed, with the latch on or off; forgetting the monster is not enough, it has not left the level (#590). 0 = the latch decides. Change together: needs caution_scary_stand = 1 (the flag is decided after each scan only there). Impact: off here; set to 1, it fires in 3 of 6 test games.

borg_param_caution_stair_parked_fallback.text: When a monster is marked on every known staircase, the stair flows go there anyway instead of finding no staircase: in town the only staircase was refused for a monster on it, harmless or long gone (#597). 0 = C. Impact: with both #597 settings on, 1 of 18 classes-18 games plays differently (a Druid, one level lower).

borg_param_caution_stair_scum_danger.text: After fleeing town, the stair scum grabs DL1 items near the stairs before going back up. 1 = skip it while the level is scary, the danger here is above caution_stair_scum_danger, or the HP is below the maximum, and go straight back up (#549). 0 = C. Impact (games of 6 that play differently with the value changed to): caution_stair_scum_threat 0: 0; caution_stair_scum_danger 1: 0.

borg_param_caution_stair_scum_threat.text: After fleeing town, the stair scum grabs DL1 items near the stairs before going back up. 1 = skip it while the level is scary, the danger here is above caution_stair_scum_danger, or the HP is below the maximum, and go straight back up (#549). 0 = C. Impact (games of 6 that play differently with the value changed to): caution_stair_scum_threat 0: 0; caution_stair_scum_danger 1: 0.

borg_param_caution_town_never_scary.text: 1 = in town no monster makes the level scary (the named list, the damage rule, the resist scares): the Borg meets town monsters by its danger rules, fights them or walks past, instead of fleeing to DL1 and coming back to finish shopping (#604, owner). The five town residents on the list (the battle-scarred veteran, the mean-looking mercenary, the filthy street urchin, the squint-eyed rogue, Farmer Maggot) made most of the town scares: at least 697 in 18 games. 0 = C. Impact: not on the file's 6-game measure; set to 1, 18 of 18 games (9 classes x seeds 2001/2002, race 0, 100,000 turns) play differently.

borg_param_caution_town_scary_levels_les.text: The scary list's level, lowered for town residents (#622, owner): a town monster on the list stops being scary this many character levels sooner, so the order stays (the veteran and the mercenary longest) and the town scare ends earlier. Higher ends it sooner: 11 or more ends the list's town scares at once (as caution_town_never_scary, but only for the list). Each level less brings more thefts (the urchin, the squint-eyed rogue): on 18 games 1 at 3, 13 at 6, 16 at 11. 0 = the list as it is. Shipped 3 (owner, 2026-11-19). Impact: not on the file's 6-game measure; on 18 classes-18 games (100,000 turns), 0: 0 deaths, sum of CL 99; 3: 0, 102; 6: 1, 99; 11: 2, 98.

borg_param_caution_twitch_avoid_lava.text: The twitch (a random step when the Borg has nothing else to do) never steps into lava without fire immunity: one step deals 100-200 fire damage (#597). 0 = C. Impact: with both #597 settings on, 1 of 18 classes-18 games plays differently; priest-809881907 lives instead of dying in lava.

borg_param_escape_fox_form.text: Fox Form for a fleeing Druid (#551). With the switch at 1, a Druid about to take a flight step at least min_steps from its goal casts Fox Form (double movement, Free Action) if its fail rate is at most fail. It keeps the shape while it flees or the level is scary. A fox does not fight: it changes back before a melee blow, and an item or a spell changes back in the same command. speed is what a fox's flight is worth in the danger and the stand decision (+10 at normal speed); stand_speed is the same for a Druid that can cast Fox Form but is not a fox yet. Raising min_steps casts on longer flights only; raising fail casts with a riskier spell; lowering the speeds counts more monsters as pursuers (more stands). 0 = never (C). Change together: these settings form one set. Impact: escape_fox_form 1: 1 of 6 test games plays differently (the Druid); the other four: 0 with the switch at 0.

borg_param_escape_phase_adjacent_rule.text: The owner's Phase Door rule (#584), at every Phase Door site (docs/PHASE-DOOR.md), before the site's own check: Phase Door only with an awake enemy on an adjacent square and the fight judged lost (lost_test). The rule only refuses the Phase Door: the other escapes go on, and if none acts the Borg attacks (its best attack; at range with nothing adjacent) or, with an awake monster in view, boosts (Speed first; else borg_defend's defences and staves). lost_test: 0 = the danger threshold below; 1 = the fight compared (its best attack of any kind, true damage, needs more turns to kill the adjacent monsters, their HP left, than the danger needs to kill it); 2 = as 1, and the expected landing is safer than here. 0 = each site's own check. Off here until a zoo pilot measures it.

borg_param_escape_phase_antisummon_delay.text: Phase Door settings of two kinds (#584; docs/PHASE-DOOR.md lists every site and its settings): - ordinary_danger_tenths, unique_danger_tenths, unique_min_count, tolerance and horizon gate escape level 3.1 only: it fires when the danger is above avoidance x ordinary_danger_tenths / 10 with no unique near (unique_danger_tenths with at least unique_min_count uniques near), and phases if at most tolerance of 100 landing grids are scary looking horizon turns ahead. Change these five together. - antisummon_delay is a shared timer, read at 7 of the 16 sites (escape 2.2, 3.1, 3.3, 4.1, 4.3, 6.1, 8): no Phase Door there for that many turns after the Borg finished a digging flow (an anti-summon corridor, or a tunnel dug straight to a monster). Impact (games of 6 that play differently with the value changed to): escape_phase_ordinary_danger_tenths 20: 0; escape_phase_unique_danger_tenths 26: 0; escape_phase_unique_min_count 4: 0; escape_phase_tolerance 50: 0; escape_phase_horizon 4: 0 (all level 3.1); escape_phase_antisummon_delay 100: 0 (the 7 sites).

borg_self_lunal.text: The borg will dive deep in the dungeon, even while he is still low level, bouncing between levels to take nearby down stairs. Once deep, he will gather items, then recall to town. He will not recall back down into the dungeon, but walk all the way down again. If you want a fast win, this is not the option for you. If you want the borg to have maxed stats early on at the expense of game turns, then give this a try. The best way to use this is to have a borg that can cast Satisfy Hunger. This is a one way trip for the borg and he will be getting hungry. The borg should also have a perma light source (like the phial). Again, one way trip. He won't be stopping to restock his fuel source. However, if he has food or fuel, he will use them when appropriate. Having extra speed will help the borg too. Often he will come down the stairs, and find himself right next to a monster. Sometimes, that monster can get the first hit on a borg, killing him instantly. Even +3 speed would help to avoid this type of instadeath. Self Lunal Mode will allow the borg to use the stair scumming in order to dive deep in the dungeon for his own goals. For example, if the borg has been down to depth 99, and now has no more potions of healing, he will only be prepared for depth 45. He will remain shallow in the dungeon, from depth 1-10 waiting for the shops to cycle. Then he will attempt to buy a healing potion from the town shops. If none is available, he will return to the shallow dungeon depths and wait for the shops to cycle. He will repeat this pattern until he gets a potion of healing. If the borg is allowed to self-lunal, then it will bounce the stairs down to a depth where it feels comfortable. In the case above, it will do this until about depth 40.

Since #479 the borg-zoo#170 speed30 bundle; borg_trip_unknown_stacks = 2 since fba1c6e0 (owner). Impact (games of 6 that play differently with the value changed to): trip_policy 0: 3; trip_pack_slack 2: 0; trip_unknown_stacks 4: 3; trip_return_gold 1: 6; trip_depth_margin 1: 0.

borg_uses_dynamic_calcs.text: Use the FORMULA SECTION below. If false the borg will use the calcs in the C code. Which is recommended since those are honed more frequently than the dynamic calcs. Most borg users will have more successful borgs by leaving this option as FALSE. note: the dynamic calcs are slower than the internal calcs

borg_uses_swaps.text: Carry swap items (equipment with a needed resist) and wear one when in danger; lets it dive deeper, at two pack slots each. Impact: set to FALSE, 0 of 6 test games play differently.

borg_verbose.text: TRUE makes the Borg note far more of its actions and thoughts.

borg_worships_ac.text: Kept from the C Borg's borg.txt: equipment taste, risk, swaps, chests, enchanting. None is tuned by this project yet. Worship: extra value for equipment that improves one attribute (an AC worshipper scores a point of AC at 3000 instead of 2000), so it trades other qualities for it. borg_worships_gold also sells everything, even unidentified, and climbs rather than recalls to sell (no effect after CL20).
